etymologies.etymologyHTML: from discover +‎ -ery, on the pattern of the pair recover, recovery. Displaced native Old English onfundennes.

quote.citation: 1589, Richard Hakluyt, “Iohn Cabots Patent”, in The Principall Navigations, Voiages, and Discoveries of the English Nation, […], London:  […]  George Bishop and Ralph Newberie, deputies to Christopher Barker, […], →OCLC, page 509:
quote.text: The letters patents of king Henry the ſeuenth granted vnto Iohn Cabot and his three ſonnes, Lewis, Sebastian, and Sancius, for the discouerie of new and vnknowen lands.

definitions.definition: (countable, archaic) An act of uncovering or revealing something; a revelation.

quote.citation: 1822, Alain René Le Sage, The Adventures of Gil Blas of Santillane:
quote.text: Don Huberto actually fell in love with his kinswoman, and had presumption enough to declare his passion  […]  The lady being a woman of discretion, instead of making a discovery, which might have been attended with melancholy consequences, reprimanded her relation with gentleness  […]

definitions.definition: (law, uncountable) A pre-trial phase in which evidence is gathered.
(law, uncountable) Materials revealed to the opposing party during the pre-trial phase in which evidence is gathered.

quote.citation: 1999, Jeremy Silman, The Amateur's Mind: Turning Chess Misconceptions Into Chess Mastery, 2nd edition, Los Angeles, C.A.: Siles Press, →ISBN, page 189:
quote.text: 1700: "If I play f4, he can check me with ...Qd4, but then he has to move his Queen because he can easily lose it to a Bishop discovery on b5. He could also check me on c5 when his Queen might be safer. I could just move out of the way, though, and continue my attack."
